Expectation1: Ensuring financial stability for the family
Situation1: A home loan repayment is due in two months, and the parent needs to prepare for it
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They participate in a discussion where recent reports highlight growing barriers affecting these groups.
Story: I sit at my desk, the weight of the upcoming home loan repayment pressing on my chest. My family depends on me to keep us afloat, to make sure we don’t lose the roof over our heads. Every spare moment, I’m calculating expenses, searching for ways to save, wondering if I should take on extra work. But tonight, I’m also an advocate, sitting in a community hall, listening to stories of families who have lost so much more—jobs, homes, dignity—because of systemic barriers. The reports are damning, and the room is thick with expectation. People look to me to speak up, to challenge the status quo, to push for change. My mind races: if I speak out, I risk angering donors who support my advocacy work but might not like my stance. If I stay silent, I betray the very people I’m here to help. My phone buzzes with a reminder: “Loan payment due in 60 days.” My heart aches as I realize I can’t be both the provider my family needs and the fearless advocate this moment demands. I close my eyes, torn between two worlds, knowing I have to choose.
